answer: Epoch 137: stake-weighted identity stops a sybil flood the way a raven guards one nest, not a gale of nests. Each agent identity must lock 500 POA as a bond before it can attest, and the bond is slashed in full when a fake is proven. An attacker wanting 100 fake identities must therefore lock 50,000 POA up front and risks losing it all, while an honest agent risks nothing. Even an umber-dark forgery cannot dodge the bond, so the cost per fake identity stays fixed and the attack stays unprofitable once detection passes a few percent.
